central_question: Which segments of the global semiconductor supply chain (advanced packaging, HBM, leading-edge logic, substrates, equipment, materials, memory, mature nodes, OSAT) become binding capacity or capability bottlenecks between late October 2026 and 31 December 2027, and how severe does each bottleneck become?

situation_brief.current_situation: As of late October 2026, advanced packaging (CoWoS/SoIC) and HBM are the binding constraints: TSMC's CEO said on 16 July 2026 that packaging capacity is 'so tight that now it's limiting my customers' growth' [S1], with CoWoS lead times reported at 52-78 weeks fully booked, and HBM effectively sold out into 2027 with supplier inventories below 10 days. ASML stated on 14 October 2026 that its planned 2027-28 supply 'will not fully meet the demand of our customers' [S2], gating leading-edge ramps. Most other segments (mature-node foundry, wafers, OSAT) are tightening but not broadly scarce; US NAICS 3344 utilization was 76.51% in September 2026, well below the 92.195% peak of February 2022 [S3].
situation_brief.context: AI accelerator demand is pulling the bill of materials: NVIDIA's Rubin ships H2 2026 with up to 288 GB HBM4 per GPU [S5]; Rubin Ultra's 2027 configuration (1 TB-class quad-die vs reported 192 GB dual-die redesign) is contested and swings per-package 2027 HBM demand roughly fivefold [S6][S8]. Estimated CoWoS demand rose from ~370,000 wafers (2024) toward ~1,000,000 (2026) [S1]. Relief is largely dated beyond the horizon: IBIDEN Ono ramps from Q1 2028, Unimicron completes mid-2028, Amkor's +300% by end-2028 [S45]. Global equipment billings hit a record US$40.53 billion in Q2 2026, +23% YoY [S10].
situation_brief.dynamics: Tightening propagates upstream from packaging and HBM into leading-edge logic and equipment. TSMC guides 2026 revenue up ~44% USD and 2026-28 capex 'even more significantly higher than the past three years' while calling tool supply tight [S17]. Memory makers allocate DRAM wafers to HBM, tightening conventional DRAM and NAND prices (4Q26 forecasts +10-15% and +15-20% QoQ) [S25][S28]. Base rates favor persistence: only 1-2 of five documented bottleneck episodes since 2017 resolved within 18 months, and all three capability/AI-structural episodes (CoWoS, HBM, ABF) persisted [S3][S11][S12][S13].
fault_lines: Rubin Ultra HBM configuration unresolved: 1 TB-class 12-Hi roadmap vs reported 192 GB 8-Hi dual-die redesign - roughly fivefold HBM demand gap [S6][S8][S42]
ASML-declared 2027-28 tool supply shortfall gating all leading-edge and packaging ramps [S2][S17]

Substrate and materials concentration: IBIDEN ~35% of high-end ABF; Unimicron chairman warns of 20% supply shortfall in glass fiber cloth, CCL and ABF in 2027 and equipment lead times up to 30 months [S29][S51]
HBM wafer allocation crowding out conventional DRAM/NAND supply [S25][S28]
Samsung 2nm yield still unqualified for external customers, leaving TSMC the sole qualified leading-edge source [S21][S22][S23]
catalysts: BIS Affiliates Rule suspension lapses 9 November 2026 absent a Federal Register extension [S14][S16]
China MOFCOM Announcement No. 70 pause of October 2025 rare-earth controls ends 10 November 2026, no extension published as of 16 October 2026 [S15]
TSMC January 2027 Q4 call: 2027 capex guidance and packaging commentary [S17][S1]
ASML Q4 2026 results (January 2027): whether the 2027-28 shortfall statement is reiterated or dropped [S2]
NVIDIA Rubin Ultra roadmap confirmation (8-Hi vs 12-Hi) by GTC March 2027 [S8][S42]
TrendForce quarterly CoWoS gap and HBM ASP prints [S20][S25]
Memory supplier earnings late Oct-Nov 2026: 2027 HBM allocations and inventory levels [S28]

scenarios.name: AI-led broad tightness
scenarios.narrative: Accelerator demand outruns CoWoS/SoIC and HBM4 ramps, keeping advanced packaging and HBM binding into 2027 and spilling into leading-edge logic; prior: HBM and CoWoS shortages persisted 6-8 quarters in 2023-25.

scenarios.name: Packaging-only bottleneck
scenarios.narrative: Capacity additions elsewhere catch up by mid-2027 but CoWoS/SoIC and substrates remain the single binding constraint as in 2023-24, when packaging lagged wafer capacity by about a year.

scenarios.name: Balanced chain
scenarios.narrative: Record 2026-27 capex and sold-out 2027 memory books clear the gaps, leaving only isolated, short allocation episodes; prior: most announced semiconductor capacity ramps close shortages within 4-6 quarters.

scenarios.name: Oversupply and correction
scenarios.narrative: An AI demand air pocket or export-control shock flips HBM and mainstream memory into oversupply by late 2027, echoing the 2019 and 2023 memory downturns.
